pages.text: "Mumu, I'll dry you!" Big sister Dodo ran to the oven. Little brother Mumu had returned from the snowy yard with damp feathers. He shivered by the oven.
"I know! Rub hard, dry fast." Dodo scrubbed his back feathers with her beak. Feathers stuck out everywhere, making him look like a chestnut burr.
"Ouch!" One feather came out. Mumu opened his beak wide and squeezed his eyes shut. Dodo lifted her beak from his back, eyes growing round. "Oh... did I hurt you?"
Mom hugged Mumu warmly in both wings. "Preen wet feathers gently. Hard rubbing hurts and ruffles them more." Looking at Dodo, she said, "Feathers, gently!"
Mom preened his feathers gently in their growing direction. One by one, ruffled feathers lay straight. Dodo watched. "Oh... gently, along the feathers!"
Now Dodo's turn. She preened Mumu's wing feathers very gently with her beak. Softly, softly. His eyes slowly closed. "Dodo, it doesn't hurt at all."
"Feathers, gently!" Dodo finished his back, following the feathers. Damp feathers dried softly in the oven glow. One flick of her tail.
Dodo sat Mumu on the chair closest to the oven. "Little brother gets warm first. I'll sit here. Maybe my beak was a broom earlier!" Dodo laughed first.

Now Dodo knew big-sister rules. "One, gently along the feathers! Two, warm place for little brother first! Three, all dry, a hug!" Next day, when Mumu came back wet, she touched her beak gently to him.

Mom hugged one child in each wing. "Our Dodo, a real big sister!" Even a strong beak feels cozy when used gently along feathers. Dodo softly touched her beak to Mumu's cheek and whispered, "Feathers, gently!"
